scenes.text: Mid-way through round two, it becomes clear to everyone in the front three rows that {subject.first} has shit {him}self. The cameras haven't noticed yet. Blow Hogan has. Blow Hogan is gagging on air.

choices.label: Tell production to stay on the wide shot
choices.result: The wide shot holds. Twitter does not. #CodeBrown trends in four countries.

choices.label: Let the cameras get it. It's content.
choices.result: Lon Anik, live: 'That is... that is a man fighting through something.' Blow Hogan, live: 'HE SHIT HIS SHORTS, LON.'

scenes.text: A memorabilia dealer wants to buy {subject.first}'s fight shorts. Unwashed. He's offering {$fee}. He says he has 'a buyer in Dubai who is very specific.'
scenes.speaker: a man named Glen

choices.label: Sell the fucking shorts
choices.result: The shorts sell. {subject.first} finds out from a TikTok. {He} has questions. You have no answers.

choices.label: Hell no. Burn them.
choices.result: You burn them in the parking lot. The smell is biblical. {subject.first} salutes.

scenes.text: {subject.first} is 1.4 pounds over with forty minutes to go. {His} cutman has a plan: 'Spit, sweat, shit. In that order.' {subject.first} is crying. The hotel toilet is crying.
scenes.speaker: the hotel bathroom

choices.label: Strip naked, towel up, try again
choices.result: {He} makes it on the nose, buck naked, behind a towel held by two very unhappy interns.

choices.label: Bribe the guy holding the scale ({$fee})
choices.result: The scale reads 'on weight.' It also reads 'on weight' when you step on it. Concerning.

scenes.text: {subject.first} has launched a subscription page. The bio reads: 'Uncensored training. Uncensored recovery. Uncensored everything. You know what the fuck this is.' It has 9,000 subscribers in a day.

choices.label: Demand a cut. It's your brand.
choices.result: Legal drafts a revenue share agreement. Legal does not make eye contact with anyone for a week.

choices.label: It's {his} body, {his} business
choices.result: One sponsor pulls out. Wrong choice of words. One sponsor leaves.

scenes.text: A clip from {subject.first}'s page has leaked to every group chat in the sport. It's just {him} doing an ice bath while reading the promotion's pay scale out loud and laughing.

choices.label: Give {him} a raise. Quietly.
choices.result: The laughing stops. The page posts a thank-you video. Fully clothed. Weirdly more threatening.

choices.label: Go on a podcast and call it fake
choices.result: It is not fake. The podcast host plays it back to you. On air.

scenes.text: Your ring card girls have unionized. Their spokesperson, Destiny, drops a list on your desk: 'Pay, a heated dressing room, and if one more drunk motherfucker in row two grabs my ass, I'm walking the card into the cage and hitting him with it.'
scenes.speaker: Destiny, Ring Card Union Local 1

choices.label: Agree to everything ({$fee})
choices.result: Security gets a new policy: 'Grab, and you get grabbed.' Row two behaves for the first time in history.

choices.label: Replace them with the interns in bikinis
choices.result: The interns are a disaster. One trips into the cage. One quits mid-walk. One is now dating the heavyweight champion.

scenes.text: A condom brand called Rubber Ducky Extra Large wants the center of the octagon. Their tagline: 'For when you're the main event.' They're offering {$fee} and want the ring girls to throw samples into the crowd.
scenes.speaker: Rubber Ducky marketing

choices.label: Take the fucking money
choices.result: The canvas logo is a giant winking duck. A fighter gets knocked out face-first directly on the duck. It becomes the photo of the year.

choices.label: Family-friendly brand, mate
choices.result: Your network calls to say thanks. Then calls back to ask if the duck people have a number.

scenes.text: Cleaning crew found a bag of white powder in {subject.first}'s locker. Taped to it: a note that says 'PRE-WORKOUT (SPECIAL)'. The commission's surprise testing team arrives tomorrow.

choices.label: Flush it and say nothing
choices.result: The toilet clogs. The plumber finds it. The plumber now has leverage.

choices.label: Hand it to the commission
choices.result: The commission thanks you for your integrity and opens an investigation into your integrity.

scenes.text: The plumber, Rick, would like {$fee}, two cageside seats and 'a picture with the bald guy who screams.' Otherwise he'd like to talk to a reporter.
scenes.speaker: Rick (plumbing, extortion)

choices.label: Pay Rick
choices.result: Rick gets his picture with Blow Hogan. Blow Hogan talks to him about elk for forty minutes. Rick considers this a fair trade.

choices.label: Tell Rick to go fuck himself
choices.result: Rick goes to a reporter. The headline is 'PLUMBER BLOWS LID OFF PROMOTION'S PIPES.' You hate how good that headline is.

scenes.text: Two very large men in very small tracksuits are in your office. They represent a 'sports investment collective' to whom {subject.first} owes {$fee}. They'd like {him} to lose on Saturday. 'Round two would be nice. We're not animals.'
scenes.speaker: the Tracksuit Brothers

choices.label: Call the commission
choices.result: The Tracksuit Brothers leave politely. Your car is egged that night. With ostrich eggs. That's a message.

choices.label: Pay the debt from {his} purse
choices.result: Debt cleared. {subject.first} hugs you and whispers 'I owe other guys too.' Fuck.

choices.label: Say nothing. Book the fight. Bet on round two.
choices.result: Round two. On the nose. You feel nothing. Then you feel everything at 3 a.m.

scenes.text: You wake up in a hotel suite in a city you don't remember flying to. There is a tiger cub in the bathtub, a signed contract for a fight in Turkmenistan on the nightstand, and a woman named Crystal asleep on the championship belt. Your phone has 41 missed calls from the owner.

choices.label: Honour the Turkmenistan contract
choices.result: The event happens. The president of Turkmenistan fights on the undercard. He wins. He was always going to win.

choices.label: Rip it up, return the tiger, call the owner
choices.result: The tiger goes back to a man named Doug. You do not ask how Doug got a tiger. Crystal keeps the belt for a week.

scenes.text: The ceremonial weigh-in venue fell through. The only room available on Friday is a funeral home. There is a viewing in the next room. 'Very quiet family,' says the director. 'They won't mind if you keep it down.'
scenes.speaker: Peaceful Pines Funeral Home

choices.label: Book it. Ask the fighters to keep it down.
choices.result: The fighters do not keep it down. A heavyweight screams 'I'M GONNA PUT YOU IN THE GROUND' and a very old man in the next room gives a thumbs up.

choices.label: Do it in the hotel parking lot instead
choices.result: It rains. Everyone weighs in wet. Three fighters miss weight because of their soaked underwear.

scenes.text: Cageside, {subject.first}'s mother and {other.first}'s mother are fighting. Real punches. Earrings off. Someone's wig is in the cage. Security is losing. The crowd is chanting 'MOM! MOM! MOM!'

choices.label: Book the moms on the next card
choices.result: The commission says 'absolutely fucking not'. The moms do it at the after-party anyway. Bigger gate than your co-main.

choices.label: Separate them and comp their tickets for life
choices.result: Both moms send you a fruit basket. Both baskets contain a threat.

scenes.text: Your cutman Eddie has been selling bloody gauze from fights on eBay. 'AUTHENTIC MAIN EVENT BLOOD, CERTIFICATE INCLUDED.' Four-thousand five-star reviews. One review says 'tastes legit.'

choices.label: Fire Eddie
choices.result: Eddie opens a competing store. 'BLOOD THE PROMOTION DOESN'T WANT YOU TO SEE.' It sells better.

choices.label: Take it in-house. Official merch.
choices.result: 'Officially licensed blood' is a sentence you have now said in a board meeting. The board loved it.

scenes.text: The owner takes you to a steakhouse, orders for both of you, and says: 'Fighters are like steaks. You beat the shit out of them until they're tender and then you charge whatever the fuck you want.' He's waiting for you to laugh.
scenes.speaker: the owner

choices.label: Laugh. Loudly. Toast to it.
choices.result: You laugh. He laughs. The waiter, a former amateur fighter, spits in your steak. You deserve it.

choices.label: 'They're people, sir.'
choices.result: He stares at you for nine seconds. 'People are also steaks.' He picks up the check. You are not sure if that's a threat.

scenes.text: Marketing has made a mascot: 'Knuckles the Concussed Kangaroo.' It wobbles around, falls down, and asks fans what year it is. Kids love it. Neurologists have sent a letter. A long letter. With diagrams.
scenes.speaker: the marketing department

choices.label: Keep Knuckles
choices.result: Knuckles merch outsells three of your champions. The neurologists' letter is framed in the break room.

choices.label: Retire Knuckles
choices.result: Knuckles' final appearance is a slow, dignified walk into a dumpster. A child cries. Marketing cries harder.

scenes.text: {reporter.name} asks if your promotion is 'a legitimate sport or just a really violent pyramid scheme.' The room goes silent. Your fighters are looking at you. The live stream has 80,000 people on it.

choices.label: 'Go fuck yourself, next question.'
choices.result: It becomes the most-quoted line in the history of the sport. A sponsor puts it on a T-shirt. Without asking. You sue. You lose. You buy the shirt.

choices.label: Answer seriously and calmly
choices.result: It is a calm, measured answer. Nobody clips it. The clip of the reporter's question gets 4 million views.

scenes.text: A heckler in row two has spent the whole night yelling things at {subject.first} about {his} mother, {his} hairline and {his} 'little baby wrestler ankles.' {subject.first} just won by knockout and is now climbing the cage. Toward row two.

choices.label: Let {him} go. The crowd's earned it.
choices.result: {subject.first} doesn't hit him. {He} just stands over him, takes his nachos, and eats them while staring. The heckler has never been so afraid.

choices.label: Security! Grab {him}!
choices.result: It takes six security guards and the referee. The heckler is escorted out for his own protection. He's crying. He's still heckling.

scenes.text: A men's health clinic will sponsor your entire prelim card if one fighter gets a vasectomy live on the pre-show. 'Snip City.' They offer {$fee}. They've already built the set.
scenes.speaker: Snip City Men's Clinic

choices.label: Find a volunteer
choices.result: A journeyman with eleven kids volunteers before you finish the sentence. The pre-show does a 2.1 rating. 'Snip City' becomes a chant.

choices.label: No. Just no.
choices.result: They take the deal to your rival. Your rival's prelim fighter screams so loud the network cuts to an infomercial.

scenes.text: Someone leaked the executive group chat. Highlights include you calling the commission 'a bunch of clipboard-sucking fucks', the owner calling the fans 'wallets with feelings', and someone in marketing posting a photo of their ass with the caption 'Q3 projections.'

choices.label: Deny everything. Blame Russian hackers.
choices.result: The Russian hackers issue a statement denying it. It's somehow the most embarrassing part.

choices.label: Own it. Apologise. Fire marketing.
choices.result: Marketing's ass becomes a meme. Marketing gets hired by your rival. Marketing is thriving.

scenes.text: Your matchmaker says the referee assigned to the main event is 'absolutely shitfaced' in the hotel bar and is currently trying to fight a ficus. The commission can't send a replacement in time.
scenes.speaker: your matchmaker

choices.label: Black coffee, cold shower, pray
choices.result: He refs the main event with sunglasses on. He stops the fight perfectly. He then falls out of the cage. Somehow it's the best officiated fight of the year.

choices.label: Complain to the commission
choices.result: They send a backup ref: a 74-year-old who last reffed in 1996. The fight goes the distance. So does his nap.

scenes.text: The singer hired for the anthem is drunk. She's halfway through a version that's mostly moaning and the word 'freedom' four times. Then she says 'fuck yeah, America' into the mic and drops it. The crowd is going nuts.

choices.label: Book her for every event
choices.result: 'Fuck Yeah America Lady' becomes a recurring segment. She has an agent now. Her rider demands a bottle of Fireball and a stool.

choices.label: Apologise to the network
choices.result: The network accepts. Privately, the network says it was the best ratings minute of the night.

scenes.text: At the face-off, {subject.first} leans in and tells {other.first} something nobody hears. {other.first} goes white, then red, then throws a chair, a water bottle and a smaller fighter. Later, the mic reveals what was said: '{other.first}, your wife says hi. She says hi a lot.'

choices.label: Run it in every promo
choices.result: The PPV sells like fucking crack. {other.first}'s wife posts a statement: 'I do say hi a lot. I'm friendly.' It doesn't help.

choices.label: Fine {subject.first} and cut the audio
choices.result: The audio leaks anyway. Lip readers on Reddit reconstruct it in eleven minutes.

scenes.text: {subject.first}'s urine sample came back... pregnant. The commission would like to know whose piss this is. {subject.first} says, and this is a direct quote, 'I don't know, my cousin's?'

choices.label: Back {his} story. Somehow.
choices.result: The cousin is subpoenaed. The cousin is very pregnant and very angry.

choices.label: Cooperate fully
choices.result: {subject.first} is suspended. {His} cousin sends you a baby shower invitation. You go. It's awkward.

scenes.text: A man in a black Abibas tracksuit and a beanie (indoors, in July) is leaning on {subject.first}'s car in the gym lot. "Jimmy Quavo. Everybody knows me. Your boy looks flat, boss. I got vitamins. Special vitamins. The kind with a needle."
scenes.speaker: Jimmy Quavo

choices.label: Run him off the property
choices.result: Jimmy shrugs, says "I'll be around," and leaves in a Hyundai with three different hubcaps.

choices.label: Look the other way
choices.result: {subject.first} starts showing up to practice looking like a different, larger person. Nobody asks. Everybody knows.

choices.label: Call the commission on him
choices.result: The commission takes a report. Jimmy finds out who made it. Jimmy always finds out.

scenes.text: Random test, 6 a.m. {subject.first}'s sample comes back lit up like a Christmas tree: three steroids, a horse dewormer and something the lab calls 'honestly impressive'. {He} says it was a bad batch of 'vitamins' from 'some guy named Jimmy'.
scenes.title: COMMISSION: ADVERSE FINDING

choices.label: Accept the suspension
choices.result: Six months. {subject.first} posts a sunset and the words 'God's plan'.

choices.label: Blame contaminated beef jerky
choices.result: The jerky company releases a statement. It is extremely angry. The suspension is shorter. The memes are eternal.

scenes.text: Jimmy Quavo is in your office. You did not let him in. Nobody let him in. "No hard feelings, boss. Business is business. I got a new product, totally undetectable, the commission can't even spell it." He puts a cooler bag on your desk.
scenes.speaker: Jimmy Quavo

choices.label: Throw the cooler bag out the window
choices.result: It lands on a commissioner's car. Somehow this helps you.

choices.label: Keep the bag. For research.
choices.result: The bag hums. You put it in the break-room fridge and label it 'DO NOT'.
